<!-- The search is progressively enhanced: all entries remain readable without JS.
To add an item, duplicate a resource-card div, give it a unique ID, and edit
data-category. Search automatically includes all visible text in the card.
For downloads, add files/topic.pdf and link to it inside the relevant card. -->
<div class="resource-tools" id="resource-tools" hidden>
  <div class="resource-search">
    <label for="resource-search">Find something useful</label>
    <input id="resource-search" type="search" placeholder="Search notes, topics, or formats…" aria-controls="resource-library">
  </div>
  <div class="resource-category">
    <label for="resource-category">Show</label>
    <select id="resource-category" aria-controls="resource-library">
      <option value="all">Everything</option>
      <option value="study">Study sheets</option>
      <option value="documents">Documents</option>
      <option value="collections">Collections</option>
    </select>
  </div>
</div>
<p class="resource-count" id="resource-count" role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" hidden></p>

[01 / Study sheet]{.eyebrow}

## The one-page study sheet

A reusable structure for turning a big topic into a concise reference.

[Study]{.tag} [Template]{.tag}

<details>
<summary>Open the study-sheet template</summary>

### Topic & purpose

Name the topic and the question this sheet should help answer.

### Core ideas

List three to five essential concepts. Define each in plain language.

### Worked example

Include one example from start to finish, with the reasoning between steps.

### Watch out for

Note common mistakes, assumptions, and exceptions.

### Test yourself

Write a few questions you can answer without looking at the sheet.

</details>

:::: {.resource-card #reading-notes data-category="documents"}
[02 / Document]{.eyebrow}

## Reading notes that stick

A simple way to capture what matters from a book, paper, or article.

[Reading]{.tag} [Notes]{.tag}

<details>
<summary>Open the reading-note template</summary>

### Source

Record the title, author, publication date, and a source link.

### The central idea

Summarize the argument in your own words, in two or three sentences.

### Evidence & questions

What supports the argument? What assumptions or questions remain?

### Connections

How does this connect with something you already know?

### Put it to use

Name one practical application or next step.

</details>
::::

:::: {.resource-card #learning-map data-category="collections"}
[03 / Collection]{.eyebrow}

## A map for learning something new

A lightweight framework for organizing a topic before diving in.

[Learning]{.tag} [Planning]{.tag}

<details>
<summary>Open the learning-map template</summary>

### Start with a destination

Define something specific you want to understand or be able to do.

### Find the foundations

List the prerequisites, key terms, and a small set of reliable starting sources.

### Learn by making

Choose a small exercise or project that puts the ideas into practice.

### Keep a question list

Collect points of confusion as you go. Revisit them after each session.

### Share a useful artifact

Create a short explanation, example, or reference sheet for someone following behind you.

</details>

::: {.shelf-note}
**A note about this shelf**

Learning is better when it's shared. These starter templates are here to be useful; as the collection grows, each entry can become a note, a download, or a link to something worth reading.
:::

```{=html}
<script>
(() => {
  const search = document.getElementById('resource-search');
  const category = document.getElementById('resource-category');
  const cards = [...document.querySelectorAll('.resource-card')];
  const count = document.getElementById('resource-count');
  const empty = document.getElementById('resource-empty');
  const update = () => {
    const terms = search.value.trim().toLocaleLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
    let visible = 0;
    cards.forEach(card => {
      const text = card.textContent.toLocaleLowerCase();
      const matches = terms.every(term => text.includes(term)) &&
        (category.value === 'all' || card.dataset.category === category.value);
      card.hidden = !matches;
      if (matches) visible++;
    });
    count.textContent = `${visible} of ${cards.length} resources`;
    empty.hidden = visible !== 0;
  };
  document.getElementById('resource-tools').hidden = false;
  count.hidden = false;
  search.addEventListener('input', update);
  category.addEventListener('change', update);
  update();
})();
</script>
```
